title: My Saviour and My King
description: My Saviour and My King in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 45, part 1, headed “The glory of Christ; the success of the gospel; and the Gentile church”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My Sa-viour and my King, Thy beau-ties are di-vine; Thy lips with bless-ings o-ver-flow, And ev-ery grace is thine.

lines: And ride in majesty to spread
Thy laws, O God, are right;
His Spirit, like a joyful oil,
Like a fair bride in rich attire,
Forsake thy gods, thy idol gods,
And pay thy Lord thy vows.
O let thy God and King
Thy children shall his honours sing

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
